mechanism: First, note the Gram target permits H = 1 (1 ≤ H ≤ N), so window averaging buys nothing: the estimate is pointwise-strength on the scalar face |H_{k,n}| = |C − 2E| ≪ X_n^{1/2+ε}, and any dispersion must run over internal variables of H itself. Step (i), exact rewrite: Abel-telescope the Mertens-weighted reciprocal family. Since M(d) − M(d−1) = μ(d), E(x) reindexes exactly (this is an identity, so the C − 2E correlation is preserved) as Σ_{d≤n} μ(d)·err(x/d) plus explicit boundary terms, where err(t) = π-count minus Li on the nested prefix, and at complete-square samples ⌊√X_n⌋ = n exactly, so the hyperbola fold at d = n has no sawtooth ψ(√x) boundary defect. Simultaneously prime-index the combined weight: H = Σ_{n<q≤x} w(q) + exact centering, w(q) = c_q − 2M(⌊x/q⌋) − 2λ(q), with c_q the per-prime comb weight read off the kernel-checked identity for C and λ smooth — C and E never separate. Step (ii), one Cauchy–Schwarz applied only in the outer wheel-frequency variable (nonzero frequencies mod Q_k, the zero mode being removed exactly by the ρ < 1/6 contraction), never between the μ-weight and the discrepancy. Step (iii), diagonal: the resulting diagonal is the variance V(x) = Σ_q w(q)², which is exactly the quantitative form of the route doc's observed C ≈ 2E correlation; the diagnostics' positive correlation is the claim V(x) ≪ x^{1+ε}. Step (iv), off-diagonal: pairs (q₁,q₂) satisfy m(q₁) − m(q₂) = (x mod q₂) − (x mod q₁) with m(q) = q⌊x/q⌋ ∈ (x−q, x], so off-diagonal pairs live on shifted hyperbolas d₁q₁ − d₂q₂ = h; for fixed h this is a congruence family d₁q₁ ≡ h (mod q₂) with moduli the primes q₂ themselves and divisor-bounded multiplicity — Deshouillers–Iwaniec/Weil territory (shifted-convolution with Kloosterman completion), not Bombieri–Vinogradov. Step (v), induction: in telescoped form the off-diagonal reduces to twisted Möbius Dirichlet-polynomial sums Σ_{d≤n} μ(d) d^{−1/2−iτ} at length n ≤ √X_n, and the verified inequality √W_k < W_{k-1} (k ≥ 3) puts every such d strictly in earlier blocks, so a strengthened inductive hypothesis B(k−1) — bilinear/exponential-sum control of μ up to L_k = W_{k-1}, not pointwise M bounds — feeds the dispersion at scale X_n without the circularity of obstacle 4. The closing bound is |H_{k,n}| ≪ x^{max(3/4, (1+θ)/2)+ε} where θ is the exponent carried by B(k−1); the 3/4 barrier is broken only if the off-diagonal decorrelation of nested discrepancies err(x/d₁), err(x/d₂) under the μ(d₁)μ(d₂) twist yields genuine cancellation, which is the load-bearing unverified step.
new_leverage: Three things a standard dispersion application does not have. (a) Exact main-term cancellation: the hardest step of Linnik dispersion is making the three main terms of ΣA² − 2ΣAB + ΣB² agree to square-root accuracy; here the wheel's zero-frequency self-coupling elimination (ρ_{k,n} < 1/6, kernel-checked) and the complete-square sampling (⌊√X_n⌋ = n exactly, killing the sawtooth boundary at the hyperbola fold) perform that subtraction as identities with zero analytic loss. (b) Well-founded bilinear induction: at generic x the length-√x Möbius sums appearing after telescoping live at an uncontrolled scale; on the primorial ladder √W_k < W_{k-1} (verified k ≥ 3), so they live strictly in earlier blocks — the synchronization that obstacle 1 treats as a liability becomes the recursion structure. (c) Correlation preservation as a variance: because the telescoping and prime-index rewrites are identities and Cauchy–Schwarz is applied only in the outer frequency variable, the observed C ≈ 2E correlation is converted into the dispersion diagonal V(x) = Σ_q (c_q − 2M(⌊x/q⌋) − 2λ(q))² — a concrete, numerically testable, attackable object — rather than being destroyed by triangle inequality as the packet warns.
target_estimate: Block-inductive telescoped dispersion estimate (BTD): for every ε > 0 there is C_ε such that for every k ≥ 3 and every complete-square sample x = X_n = (n+1)²−1 ∈ (W_{k-1}, W_k], assuming the bilinear inductive hypothesis B(k−1) [sup over |τ| ≤ W_k of |Σ_{d≤t} μ(d) d^{−iτ}| ≪_ε t^{θ+ε}(1+|τ|)^{o(1)} for all t ≤ L_k = W_{k-1}], the combined signed scalar satisfies |H_{k,n}| = |C_{k,n} − 2E_{k,n}| ≤ C_ε · x^{max(3/4, (1+θ)/2)+ε}. Variables: d ≤ n (all in earlier blocks), primes q ∈ (n, x], pair shift h with |h| ≤ q, moduli = the primes q₂ from off-diagonal pairs. Loss budget: x^ε from divisor multiplicities in the pair-to-congruence map; one square root from the single outer Cauchy–Schwarz (requires diagonal V(x) ≪ x^{1+ε}); the DI/Weil step must save q₂^{1/2} per modulus across the off-diagonal family. At θ = 1/2 the fixed point is 3/4 + ε (rung 1); rung 2 additionally requires the μ-twisted decorrelation of nested discrepancies, i.e. cancellation in Σ_{d≤n} μ(d) d^{−1/2−i(γ−γ′)} uniformly over the relevant spectral differences, which I flag as UNVERIFIED and the weakest link.

obstacle_positions.pinned_vs_averaged: Compatible by construction: the dispersion runs at fixed pinned x = X_n; all averaging is over internal pair variables (d1, d2, q1, q2, h), never over translates of the block start. L_k enters only through exact identities (zero-mode removal, and the verified inclusion d-range < L_k), i.e., the primorial phase is used directly, not averaged over. Residual pinned risk resurfaces in frequency space: the spectral differences gamma - gamma' in the decorrelation step are a fixed set, not an averageable family — stated plainly under self-assessed risk.
obstacle_positions.large_sieve_non_transfer: Conceded for the single wheel modulus: plain Parseval mod Q_k with Q_k > 6x has empty off-diagonal (q1 = q2 forced) and yields only the rung-0 saving. The constructed transfer this angle claims: off-diagonal pairs map to congruences d1*q1 = h (mod q2) with moduli the primes q2 in (n, x] and divisor-bounded multiplicity; sub-square multiplicity is exactly what the kill test's r(h) computation checks. This is a concrete candidate for the missing pair-to-modulus map, and it is UNVERIFIED.
obstacle_positions.not_bombieri_vinogradov: Agreed and respected: no residue-classes-to-varying-moduli input is used. The moduli that appear are generated internally by pair analysis (the primes q2), and the off-diagonal is a shifted-convolution / Kloosterman-completion problem in the Deshouillers-Iwaniec lineage, which is the correct native habitat for disjoint reciprocal intervals.
obstacle_positions.strong_induction_failure: The angle's central reply: obstacle 4 is confirmed for pointwise |M(d)| <= K d^{1/2+eps} insertion, so the inductive hypothesis is strengthened to bilinear form — Dirichlet-polynomial/exponential-sum control of mu up to L_k. The verified inequality sqrt(W_k) < W_{k-1} makes this recursion well-founded (all d <= n lie in strictly earlier blocks). Cost stated honestly: the ladder statement must be strengthened (pointwise target at block k does not obviously imply the bilinear hypothesis at block k), which changes the Lean-side interface — one proves a stronger statement to close the induction.
obstacle_positions.parity: The angle operates in type-II/bilinear format with mu-signs as active weights, the standard parity-breaking configuration (Friedlander-Iwaniec); it never reduces to a sieve upper bound on |mu|-support, so classical parity does not bind as stated. Discipline required: if the off-diagonal is ever majorized by absolute values, the argument degenerates to sieve-type information and the parity wall reappears; the design rule is that every reduction step must be an identity or a signed estimate.
obstacle_positions.finite_range_deception: Numerics are used only for falsification (kill tests), never as evidence of an exponent. The predicted 3/4 barrier is theory-derived; the empirical signature sought (mu-vs-discrepancy decorrelation, bounded r(h) multiplicity, V(x)/x^{1+eps} bounded) is structural yes/no over multiple blocks, not a fitted exponent over few dyadic scales. Passing all kill tests proves nothing and is recorded as such.

kill_test: Exact-arithmetic computation at x = X_n across blocks k = 5..8 (x up to ~10^7, feasible with a segmented sieve): (1) compute the diagonal variance V(x) = Σ_{n<q≤x} (c_q − 2M(⌊x/q⌋) − 2λ(q))² with c_q, λ read from the kernel-checked identity — if V(x)/x^{1+ε} grows clearly across blocks, the single Cauchy–Schwarz cannot close at rung 2 and the angle dies; (2) compute the pair-multiplicity r(h) = #{(q₁,q₂): (x mod q₂) − (x mod q₁) = h} — if some h carries ≫ x^{1/2} pairs, the DI off-diagonal step cannot be sub-square and the angle dies; (3) compute the sign-correlation between μ(d) and err(x/d) over d ≤ n — a systematic nonzero correlation across blocks means the μ-twist does not decorrelate the nested discrepancies and the beyond-3/4 mechanism dies. Test (3) is the cheapest (hours of compute) and the most decisive against the load-bearing step.
rung0_plan: Abel-telescoped PNT, fully unconditional: rewrite E via M(d) − M(d−1) = μ(d) into Σ_{d≤n} μ(d)·err(x/d) (an identity, so C − 2E stays combined), bound |μ| ≤ 1 and insert the Vinogradov–Korobov-strength err(t) ≪ t·exp(−c(log t)^{3/5−ε}); the sum Σ_{d≤n} (x/d)·exp(−c(log(x/d))^{3/5}) is dominated by d ~ n = ⌊√x⌋ and totals x·exp(−c′(log x)^{3/5−ε}) = o(x). The comb side C is PNT-corrected by construction, so the same input closes it. Independently, the single-modulus Parseval mod Q_k (empty off-diagonal since Q_k > 6x) gives the comb discrepancy ≤ √(|I|·π(x)) ~ x/√(log x), a second o(x) route confirming the machinery's rung-0 viability. Both use the exact zero-mode removal as given; neither requires any averaging over the pinned start.
plausible_partial: Realistically provable at bounded effort: (a) the rung-0 statement above, rigorously and uniformly over blocks and samples (classical inputs only, weeks-scale); (b) the conditional contraction step — B(k−1) at exponent θ implies the pinned bound x^{max(3/4,(1+θ)/2)+ε} at block k — i.e., a rigorous exponent-recursion whose fixed point is 3/4 + ε, isolating the beyond-3/4 gap as exactly the μ-twisted decorrelation of nested discrepancies (rung 1 at θ = 3/4 + ε, conditional on the strengthened induction being formalizable); (c) unconditionally, a power-saving equidistribution of x mod q over primes q ∈ (x^{1/2}, x^{2/3}] via Vinogradov/van der Corput on Σ ψ(x/q), giving a fixed θ < 1 for the unweighted model comb (M replaced by bounded weights). I do not consider rung 2 plausibly provable at bounded effort by this angle alone.
self_assessed_risk: The assumption most likely false: that the off-diagonal decorrelation — cancellation in Σ_{d≤n} μ(d) d^{−1/2−iτ} uniformly over the pinned spectral differences τ = γ − γ′ that the nested discrepancies err(x/d) generate — can be obtained from earlier-block information. Pointwise Mertens bounds at earlier blocks do not imply Dirichlet-polynomial bounds uniform in τ, large-values technology averages over τ while this τ-set is pinned (obstacle 1 reappearing in frequency space), and uniform control of exactly these sums is RH-adjacent; so the angle past the 3/4 barrier may be circular. Secondary risk: the diagonal claim V(x) ≪ x^{1+ε} is only supported by the route doc's finite diagnostics and could fail (kill test 1). All of this is professional speculation and UNVERIFIED.
